overlays.notes: Measured 2026-07-13 from the protocol's own stats API: total collateral value $71,324,392 against total BOLD supply 29,047,740 gives a system collateralization ratio of 2.455; Stability Pool deposits of 19,111,283 BOLD against the same supply give a liquidation capacity ratio of 0.658. The dedicated qualitative review on 2026-07-15 used Liquity's current documentation and implementation pinned at commit c8a5a4ee2e9dc024905856b6698a77d849c68c7e. Each branch has its own Stability Pool; liquidation burns deposited BOLD against debt and redistributes any remainder only among active Troves in that branch. That establishes an adequate two-stage backstop and adequate operational branch isolation, while the shared BOLD claim still exposes holders to unrecovered debt from any branch and prevents a strong rating. A branch can permanently shut down below its SCR or on oracle failure, stop interest and new borrower operations, and enable urgent branch redemptions. Liquity's own risk disclosure nevertheless states that collapsed collateral can leave unbacked BOLD with no unconditional recapitalization facility, so shutdown and bad-debt handling is limited. Any BOLD holder can permissionlessly redeem through the CollateralRegistry for a routed mix of collateral at protocol value, with urgent redemption available after branch shutdown, supporting adequate structural redemption.

TroveManager.getTCR at the canonical protocol price - an eth_call simulation of PriceFeed.fetchPrice() = 1875.88242714 USD/ETH, agreeing 0.0000% with the Chainlink ETH/USD feed - returned 5.033 (derivation check: getTCR == floor(coll x price / debt), exact). An earlier same-day read at block 25530791 used the frozen lastGoodPrice (1780.21673094, about 5.1% stale in the quiet system) and gave 4.776; superseded by owner decision D2 on 2026-07-14. StabilityPool.getTotalLUSDDeposits() over getEntireSystemDebt() gives a liquidation capacity ratio of 0.278; LUSD totalSupply() equals getEntireSystemDebt() exactly at the pinned block, so the ratio is identical against supply. checkRecoveryMode() was false, MCR 110%, CCR 150%. The pinned implementation and official documentation establish that Stability Pool deposits burn liquidated debt and that any residual debt and collateral are redistributed across active Troves, supporting an adequate backstop design while the measured 27.8% committed-capital ratio remains visible. Liquity V1 is one immutable ETH-only Trove system, so cross-branch isolation is structurally not applicable. Recovery Mode changes liquidation rules but the protocol has no shutdown or unconditional recapitalization facility, supporting limited shutdownAndBadDebt quality. Any holder can permissionlessly redeem LUSD for protocol-priced ETH from the lowest-collateralized Troves, supporting adequate structural redemption.

overlays.notes: Measured on-chain 2026-07-14 at HyperEVM block 40440545 via eth_call. The contract graph was derived on-chain: the feUSD token exposes no Liquity getters (it is a role-gated upgradeable ERC20, not Liquity's BoldToken), so the graph was taken from the CollateralRegistry proxy 0x9de1e57 (impl 0xD06DfC33), whose totalCollaterals() = 4 and getTroveManager(i)/getToken(i) enumerate exactly four branches: WHYPE (TM 0x3100F4e7), UBTC (TM 0xbbe5f227), kHYPE (TM 0x7c07bB77), wstHYPE (TM 0x58446C58). The registry address is corroborated by Felix's own docs, and each TroveManager's activePool() matches the four holders already in the coin file's liveReservesConfig. Per branch, getEntireBranchColl() x PriceFeed.lastGoodPrice() over getEntireBranchDebt(): WHYPE 430,173.636 WHYPE @ $65.20795344 = $28,050,742 vs debt 9,522,352.500 (CR 2.946); UBTC 28.055 @ $62,449.56855 = $1,752,006 vs debt 569,059.981 (CR 3.079); kHYPE 75,231.740 @ $64.98626 = $4,889,029 vs debt 1,123,782.912 (CR 4.351); wstHYPE 10,395.891 @ $65.41448 = $680,042 vs debt 348,425.553 (CR 1.952). System totals: collateral $35,371,819 over total branch debt 11,563,620.946 feUSD = collateralizationRatio 3.059. Cross-checks: (1) Felix's TroveManager has no getTCR(uint256), so collateral was verified three ways — TroveManager.getEntireBranchColl() equals ActivePool.getCollBalance() equals the collateral ERC20's balanceOf(ActivePool) for all four branches (exact, to within 1 wei on WHYPE); (2) re-valuing the same collateral at the live PriceFeed.fetchPrice() instead of lastGoodPrice() gives CR 3.070, agreeing to within 0.4%; (3) total branch debt 11,563,620.946 versus feUSD totalSupply() 11,563,588.435 agree to 0.0003% — supply is 32.51 feUSD BELOW debt, which is the expected direction for Liquity V2 (branch debt includes interest accrued but not yet minted), not a discrepancy. DefiLlama independently reports 11,563,600.69 circulating. liquidationCapacityRatio = sum of StabilityPool.getTotalfeUSDDeposits() (the fork's rename of getTotalBoldDeposits) 9,915,239.353 over total debt = 0.857; each pool's deposits plus getYieldGainsOwed() reconcile exactly against feUSD.balanceOf(StabilityPool), confirming the deposit figure is committed capital actually held, not an accounting claim. IMPORTANT QUALIFIER: Stability Pools are branch-local and cannot cross-subsidize, and coverage is very uneven — UBTC's pool holds 3.572x its own branch debt while wstHYPE holds only 0.238x and WHYPE 0.703x. Capping each branch's usable pool at its own debt gives a branch-isolation-adjusted ratio of 0.731; the reported 0.857 is the brief's uncapped sum-over-total definition and is the optimistic bound. Parameters read on-chain from each BorrowerOperations: MCR 135% / CCR 170% / SCR 120% for WHYPE, kHYPE and wstHYPE, and MCR 125% / CCR 150% / SCR 120% for UBTC. All four branches are live (shutdownTime() = 0) and on their primary oracle (PriceFeed priceSource = 0, i.e. not fallen back to lastGoodPrice). Liquidation penalties are not exposed by any public getter. Felix's docs and pinned implementation establish an independent state contract per branch, a branch-local Stability Pool with residual debt and collateral redistributed only to that branch's active troves, system redemption through the CollateralRegistry, and SCR-triggered branch shutdown with urgent redemption. Backstop and branch isolation are adequate; structural redemption is adequate. Shutdown and bad-debt handling are limited because shutdown, urgent redemption, and redistribution are implemented, but no separate recapitalization facility covers a branch-wide collateral deficit and the documented external control is Anthias monitoring.

The add-only RegisterPool history was queried from the PoolManager deployment block through the pinned block and contains exactly the two configured long pools. Both were graph-checked against PoolManager; pool debt plus legacy supply reconciled to total supply with 0.000000% divergence, and manager accounting agreed within 0.0024%. Protocol anchor-valued collateral over supply gives 1.493559. fxBASE token inventory gives 0.891605 committed liquidation capacity and agrees with share NAV within 0.0227%. Both pools were unpaused for borrowing and redemption at the pinned block. The pinned PoolManager implementation gives EMERGENCY_ROLE a protocol pause, permits a DEBT_REDUCER_ROLE to burn supplied fxUSD while reducing pool debt, and lets the short-pool counterparty settle shortfall by reducing long-pool collateral and invalidating residual credit notes. Normal redemption is disabled while paused, although counterparty-only settlement redemption remains available, and the implementation establishes no unconditional external recapitalization facility. These bounded emergency and bad-debt paths support limited shutdownAndBadDebt quality.

overlays.notes: Measured at finalized Ethereum block 25536894; journaled evidence: shared/data/safety-score-v9/mechanism-measurements/reusd-resupply/2026-07-15-block-25536894.json. The registry enumerated 19 unique pairs and their collateral vault conversions; active-pair collateral over debt gives 1.078969, with debt and token supply diverging 0.0304%. Three zero-debt pairs remain enumerated but their converted assets are excluded from the system ratio. InsurancePool reUSD held against debt gives 0.100629 committed liquidation capacity. Collateral is a layered ERC-4626 claim on crvUSD/frxUSD lending markets valued at protocol accounting par, not proof of immediate underlying liquidity. The pinned LiquidationHandler records uncovered debt by collateral and can clear it only when recovered collateral or InsurancePool assets are sufficient, while owner-directed distribution can socialize impaired collateral to InsurancePool holders; this is a defined but limited bad-debt path without unconditional recapitalization or global settlement. The pinned RedemptionHandler lets holders redeem pair debt directly only when its owner-configurable guard is disabled or the reUSD oracle price falls below the permissionless threshold; otherwise only the protocol redemption operator may call it. Same-transaction communal redemption therefore exists, but its conditional access and configurable fees support limited structural redemption.

overlays.notes: Pinned Celo block 72202914; journaled evidence: shared/data/safety-score-v9/mechanism-measurements/audm-mento/2026-07-15-block-72202914.json. The producer enumerated all 16 live exchange IDs, found the configured token/USDm pair exactly once, and measured 10000000 USDm of counter-bucket capacity at a 15 bps spread. Conversion capacity is an analogous exit metric only and is not relabeled as collateralization or liquidation capital. Completion pass 2026-07-20 (backstop, branchIsolation, shutdownAndBadDebt added; all prior components, metrics, and sources preserved and both source URLs re-fetched and re-read this session): the Celoscan page confirms the pinned contract is the verified Mento BiPoolManagerProxy, and the Mento V3 documentation establishes that Mento conversion pools quote an oracle rate through a Chainlink-only oracle path, that trading limits cap flow per token over time, and that circuit breakers trip and halt trading when stablecoins move too far off peg or other safety thresholds are breached, with USDm/EURm backed by the shared Mento Reserve. Backstop is limited: the measured 10000000 USDm virtual counter-bucket is bounded conversion inventory, and the shared reserve backing USDm is not an AUDm-dedicated committed backstop. Branch isolation is limited: per-pair buckets bound AUDm/USDm flow, but the Broker, USDm counter-asset, shared reserve, and oracle paths are failure domains shared with other Mento stables. Shutdown and bad-debt handling is limited: BreakerBox circuit breakers and trading limits can halt unsafe conversion, but no unconditional residual-deficit recapitalization or holder settlement path is documented for AUDm. No prior quality tier was changed; the added components follow the same limited pattern as sibling Mento conversion-token overlays. NOT established: any AUDm-dedicated insurance fund or stability pool, any documented reserve commitment earmarked for AUDm residual deficits, and any formal shutdown or wind-down settlement procedure for AUDm holders.

The API reported $1,903,674,277.60 total collateral against 1,226,645,029.842961 USDD total supply, giving a self-reported system collateralization ratio of 1.551936. It also reported 77,726,668.75 USDT in PSM-USDT-A, only 0.063365 of supply; this is a snapshot of direct PSM USDT inventory, not committed liquidation capital. Per-ilk minimum ratios, debt ceilings, delayed oracle routing, Dog liquidation thresholds, and Clip Dutch auctions are explicit, supporting adequate collateralization parameters and liquidation mechanics. ChainSecurity records that V2 Flop cannot mint recapitalization tokens: it can sell only JST already deposited in the contract, with no guarantee that sufficient JST will be present, and a trusted operator can withdraw that inventory. overlays.notes: Reviewed 2026-07-19 by Kimi rescue lane 1d (2026-07-19). Measured at finalized Ethereum block 25538909 (2026-07-19T03:26:15Z) via journaled eth_call plus same-day protocol API captures; evidence: shared/data/safety-score-v9/mechanism-measurements/zchf-frankencoin/2026-07-19-api-and-chain-capture.json. The eth_call totalSupply() of 30429960.649122455 ZCHF matches the protocol API's ethereum-mainnet supply at displayed precision; global supply is 34139468.87 ZCHF. System collateralization ratio 1.645315 = 56170191.00 CHF computed collateral value (open, non-denied position balances valued at price-mapping CHF prices) over total supply; the protocol's own TVL cross-check (56689834.48 CHF, 0.92% higher) gives 1.660537 and the position-debt-only variant 1.674787. Position-level parameters are explicit per the positions documentation and API: owner-set liquidation price bounding mintable debt, per-position minimum collateral, per-position reserve contribution (observed 10%-40% of minted, mostly 20%-25%), 1%-3% annual interest, and mostly one-day challenge periods; new minters pass a 14-day application with qualified pool-share holder veto (>2% of holding-period-weighted votes). No protocol-enforced minimum collateral ratio beyond the owner-set liquidation price was found; sound pricing is enforced ex-post through challenges, supporting adequate rather than strong collateralization parameters. Liquidation runs through permissionless challenge auctions whose bid-switching design (bids above the liquidation price buy the challenger's collateral instead of the position's) makes price manipulation expensive, with a 2% challenger reward and no oracle dependency: adequate liquidation mechanics whose own documentation states the assumption that challengers can acquire the collateral asset, and no committed bidder of last resort exists. Bids are externally funded and no ZCHF-dedicated pool is contractually committed to debt offset, so liquidationCapacityRatio is structurally not applicable; the measured reserve pool is loss-absorption capital and is reported as analogous metrics instead. Backstop: the reserve documentation and pinned source establish three loss layers - the challenged position's minter reserve contribution, then FPS equity, then the general minter reserve - with coverLoss minting uncovered ZCHF as the terminal backstop; at block 25538909 the reserve pool held 12748870.64 ZCHF = 37.34% of supply (minter reserve 8634455.93 = 25.29%, FPS equity 4114414.71 = 12.05%; FPS market cap about $12.34M), supporting adequate backstop. NOT established: any stress-tested bound on reserve adequacy against the tokenized-equity collateral lines (BOSS is about 31% of collateral value), and the terminal backstop is dilutive inflation rather than pre-funded capital. Branch isolation: each position is a separate contract holding exactly one collateral type, and a failed position's collateral cannot be seized for another position's debt; cross-branch transmission exists only through the shared FPS equity and general minter reserve after a position's own reserve is consumed - adequate. NOT established: any per-collateral debt ceiling limiting one collateral line's share of system debt. Shutdown and bad debt: no global settlement or shutdown mechanism exists; bad debt is socialized through coverLoss, whose pinned source shows the reserve pool absorbing first and any uncovered remainder being minted as new ZCHF - limited. Structural redemption: holders have no direct redemption claim on position collateral; structural exits are the 1:1 stablecoin bridges (XCHF/VCHF/CHFAU, per-bridge limits and horizons) and secondary markets, while auctions repay position debt rather than holder claims - limited. NOT established: any holder-level redemption path to collateral.

liquidationCapacityRatio.rationale: Frankencoin challenge auctions are funded by external bidders, not by a ZCHF-dedicated pool contractually committed to debt offset; the measured reserve pool (0.373435 of supply at block 25538909) is loss-absorption capital evidenced in the backstop component, not committed liquidation capacity.

overlays.notes: Reviewed 2026-07-20. The Parallelizer Module documentation establishes a basket conversion mechanism rather than a debt CDP: USDp is minted and burnt at oracle value against a DAO-whitelisted asset set with adaptive fees that widen as an asset depegs or exposures breach target bounds, and any holder can redeem at any time for a proportional share of the backing basket, with a dynamic penalty factor applied when the system collateral ratio falls below 100% so redemptions re-collateralize the system. The mechanism therefore has no borrower debt positions and no liquidation engine; liquidationMechanics and the liquidation capacity metric are structurally not applicable. The collateralization ratio reported is an observed issuer-dashboard measurement, not a vault TCR: Parallel's server-rendered transparency inventory fetched 2026-07-20 publishes per-asset reserve values summing to 2,066,232.71 USD (frxUSD 251,595.61; sfrxUSD 478,492.26; USDe 48.44 on Ethereum plus 134,675.69 as HyperEVM USDeOFT; sUSDe 104,829.86 on Ethereum plus 411,598.26 on HyperEVM; sUSDS 77,458.19 and USDS 19.94 on Base; USDC 15,647.77 and ygamiUSDC 591,866.70 on Avalanche) against a published total USDp supply of 1,986,639.81, a backing ratio of 1.040064. The whitelisted basket, per-asset exposure targets, and adaptive fee schedule are documented and the Ethereum Parallelizer diamond's minter role and collateral list were verified on-chain 2026-07-20, supporting adequate collateralization parameters. Permissionless anytime proportional redemption at oracle value supports adequate structural redemption, subject to the documented whitelist caveat for restricted collateral assets. The documented below-100% redemption penalty is a socialized, fee-based recapitalization path rather than an insurance fund, and pause/guardian powers sit with DAO governance and a team multisig, supporting limited shutdownAndBadDebt. NOT established: any dedicated backstop or insurance capital behind the basket (backstop left bounded); the isolation between per-chain Parallelizer baskets sharing one fungible USDp (branchIsolation left bounded); and the freshness bounds or failover behavior of the underlying Chainlink/RedStone/DIA feeds, which are scored under oracle risk.

overlays.notes: 2026-07-20 review. Zephyr Protocol is a Monero-fork chain running a Minimal-Djed reserve design: ZSD is minted and redeemed directly against the ZEPH base coin held in the on-chain protocol reserve, and ZRS reserve shares form the equity/first-loss tranche. There are no borrowing positions and no liquidations in the design — peg defense is mint gating plus an always-permitted redemption path — so the liquidationMechanics component and the liquidationCapacityRatio metric are structurally not-applicable. Whitepaper rules: new ZSD cannot be minted when the reserve ratio is below 400% (dual spot and moving-average ratios must both pass, an anti-manipulation variation on stock Djed); ZRS minting halts above 800% to prevent dilution; the ZRS price falls toward PminRC below 400% to incentivize recapitalization; redeem_stable is always permitted, paying oracle value while the reserve ratio is >= 1 and a pro-rata share of the reserve if it ever falls below 1 (stable-holder haircut as the terminal bad-debt rule). Post-audit hardfork v11 renamed asset types to ZPH/ZSD/ZRS/ZYS per the protocol documentation. MEASUREMENT from the protocol's own reserve snapshot API (captured 2026-07-19T23:46:28Z at reserve_height 822991): ZEPH reserve 4,450,016.09, ZSD circulation 422,029.10, ZRS circulation 2,632,087.36, spot price $0.46573515 per ZEPH; reserve assets = 4,450,016.09 x 0.46573515 = $2,072,528.91 against $422,029.10 ZSD liabilities (equity $1,650,499.79) giving the protocol-reported reserve_ratio of 4.910867 on spot and 4.537806 on the moving average. collateralizationRatio is reported as the spot reserve ratio 4.910867; the moving-average figure 4.537806 is the binding mint-gate value. NOT ESTABLISHED: the snapshot API is the protocol's own self-reported scanner and no independent third-party attestation of the reserve was found; the oracle operator set and its decentralization were not established; ZRS secondary-market depth (real recapitalization capacity) was not established; no shutdown or wind-down mechanism exists in the design.

liquidationCapacityRatio.rationale: Djed-style reserve design with no borrowing positions and no liquidation engine: ZSD is minted and redeemed directly against the protocol reserve under reserve-ratio gates (400% min mint, 800% max), so there is no liquidation pool whose capacity could be measured.

liquidationMechanics.rationale: No liquidation mechanism exists in the Djed-style design: there are no loans or margin positions; stability is enforced by reserve-ratio mint gates and always-permitted redemption against the protocol reserve.

branchIsolation.rationale: Single-collateral (ZEPH-only), single-reserve Djed design: there are no branches or isolated markets to segregate.

It is limited rather than adequate because no binding legal document establishes a holder claim on segregated reserve assets: the Terms of Use page is JavaScript-rendered and only its footer legal disclosure was retrievable (identifying the operating entities — Adventure One QSS Inc. internationally, and QCX LLC d/b/a Polymarket US as a CFTC-regulated Designated Contract Market for the US platform), with no trust, segregation, or bankruptcy-remoteness language for pUSD reserves located in any retrieved source. CUSTODY CONTINUITY (limited). The reserves are not held at any custodian: backing USDC/USDC.e sits in the on-chain backing vault contract 0xc417fd8e9661c0d2120b64a04bb3278c17e99db1 on Polygon, verified by eth_call at block 90551185 (2026-07-20T07:16 UTC) to hold 630,114,454.459495 USDC.e plus 313.420408 native USDC. Continuity therefore rests on immutable contract custody plus a timelocked admin — documented and on-chain verified, but with no custodian diversification and with upgrade-key risk, hence limited. ASSURANCE AND RECONCILIATION (adequate). A complete direct on-chain assets-and-liabilities reconciliation was performed at Polygon block 90551185: pUSD totalSupply 629,375,893.36934 against vault-held 630,114,767.879903 USDC-equivalent, a coverage ratio of approximately 1.00117 — every outstanding pUSD is matched by verifiable on-chain collateral with a small surplus, and this reconciliation is continuously reproducible by any party against public RPC data. In addition, the official contracts registry links two independent third-party audits of the CTF Exchange V2 system (Quantstamp and Cantina, both March 2026) and a live Cantina bug bounty. Per the on-chain reconciliation precedent this supports adequate; it is not strong because no independent financial-statement examination or attestation exists and the reconciliation here is self-performed. NOT ESTABLISHED: any legal segregation, trust, or bankruptcy-remoteness for pUSD reserves; the full Terms of Use text bearing on pUSD (page shell only was retrievable); whether the Quantstamp/Cantina reports cover the CollateralToken contract specifically (reports linked from the official docs but their per-contract scope was not re-verified); the identity/signers of the governance Safe behind the 12-hour Timelock.

overlays.notes: Measured 2026-07-20 at Ethereum block 25572058 via eth_call over https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com, cross-checked against Inverse's own stats APIs fetched the same hour (fixed-markets at 06:04:58Z, FiRM TVL at 06:11:17Z). SCOPE: DOLA issuance is FiRM-Fed dominated — the on-chain FiRM Fed (0x2b34548b865ad66a2b046cb82e59ee43f75b90fd) globalSupply() read 97,584,203.48 DOLA = 96.73% of the 100,888,118.24 DOLA totalSupply() at the same block, and the markets API reconciles exactly: sum(totalDebt) 42,982,751.71 + sum(idle market dolaLiquidity) 54,602,362.64 = 97,585,114.36, within 0.001% of globalSupply (unaccrued drip timing). The PSM Fed currently issues nothing (PSM supply() = 0). collateralizationRatio = 1.305242 = FiRM total collateral TVL $56,102,913.11 (Inverse f2/tvl API) over FiRM DOLA debt $42,982,751.71 (Inverse fixed-markets API); this is a FiRM-branch measurement — DOLA minted but sitting idle inside market contracts (54.6M) is protocol inventory, not outstanding debt, and the residual ~3.3M of legacy-Fed supply (incl. unresolved 2022 Frontier bad debt whose current amount was NOT established) carries no dedicated collateral. Analogous supply-wide ratio 0.55609 (= TVL / total DOLA supply) is reported for transparency, not used as the metric. COLLATERALIZATION PARAMETERS (adequate): every FiRM market has governance-set collateral factor, liquidation factor, liquidation incentive, minDebt, ceiling, and rolling 24h borrow limits — observed live in the API across 45 markets (collateralFactor 0.30-0.92, liquidationFactor 0.326-1.0, liquidationIncentive 0.04-0.12) and documented as market parameters in the liquidations documentation; pricing runs through the documented Pessimistic Price Oracle (lower of current Chainlink price vs 48h low), with staleness thresholds halting new borrows and an EOA/whitelist borrow gate. Parameters are governance-mutable with no third-party attestation of their adequacy, so adequate rather than strong. LIQUIDATION MECHANICS (adequate): documented permissionless third-party liquidators repay DOLA debt (up to the market liquidation factor) and seize collateral plus the market liquidation incentive; depleted-DBR positions first accrue debt via forced replenishment at a documented 54.75% APR (10% of the replenishment cost to the caller) until liquidation eligibility. Incentive parameters verified in the API; no liquidation was stress-tested this session. liquidationCapacityRatio is structurally not-applicable: FiRM liquidations are funded by external liquidators, and no DOLA-dedicated pool is contractually committed to fund liquidation repayments (the jrDOLA vault absorbs post-liquidation bad-debt shortfalls — evidenced under backstop — it does not fund liquidations). BACKSTOP (limited): jrDOLA (0x633821b8e003344e5223509277f2084ea809a452, on-chain name 'Junior Dola', asset() = sDOLA) is a documented ERC-4626 first-loss vault whose sDOLA assets the FiRMSlashingModule (0x3b1E443aB423c9A7B1B2EA7b3cB7c0be012a4FbF) can slash to repay FiRM bad debt before protocol reserves; but at block 25572058 the vault held only 438.754496 sDOLA (totalAssets) = ~614.99 DOLA, i.e. 0.00001431 of FiRM debt — the committed buffer is currently negligible. Slashing also requires a governance-or-guardian trigger, covers only governance-approved FiRM markets, and explicitly excludes the PSM; residual losses beyond the vault fall on unquantified protocol reserves. Limited for the material size/coverage gaps despite a well-documented, audited (dual Sherlock, per docs) design. BRANCH ISOLATION (adequate): documented Personal Collateral Escrows give each user a dedicated escrow per collateral market, so a compromised market cannot touch collateral in other markets; the API confirms a per-market escrowImplementation and isolated market contracts. Bad debt is still mutualized to the whole system via jrDOLA/reserves, so adequate rather than strong. SHUTDOWN AND BAD DEBT (limited): the documented path is liquidation shortfall -> jrDOLA slash -> protocol reserves, and the DBR documentation states DBR xy=k auction proceeds currently repay outstanding bad debt from the 2022 Frontier exploit (a real, documented recapitalization route, but slow and revenue-dependent); no global DOLA shutdown or holder settlement path is documented, and the current outstanding bad-debt amount was not established this session. STRUCTURAL REDEMPTION (limited): the PSM (0x4dfd662622d766304cb539e66f893c4defa19398; verified source read via Routescan) offers permissionless DOLA->USDS swaps at 1:0.998 (on-chain sellFeeBps = 20, buyFeeBps = 0, vault() = sUSDS 0xa3931d71877C0E7a3148CB7Eb4463524FEc27fbD) — but supply() read 0 at block 25572058, so current redemption capacity is zero, and USDS is external Sky collateral, not protocol collateral. No redemption of DOLA for FiRM collateral exists. NOT ESTABLISHED this session: any committed liquidation-funding pool; the size/composition of protocol reserves beyond jrDOLA; the outstanding legacy Frontier bad-debt figure; independent verification of the Inverse stats APIs' TVL/debt figures (issuer-published numbers cross-checked against on-chain Fed supply only); liquidation behavior under stress (no live or historical liquidation replay). REASSESSMENT 2026-07-22 (Pharos honesty-downgrade ruling, owner-accepted): the 2026-07-22 FiRM fixed-markets API pull pinned at Ethereum block 25584925 (see dola-inverse-finance.json reserveReview) shows FiRM's non-Frontier DOLA debt is now dominated by DOLA-paired Curve LP collateral markets (sUSDe-DOLA, yv-sUSDe-DOLA, sUSDS-DOLA, yv-sUSDS-DOLA, yv-USR-DOLA, and scrvUSD-sDOLA), which together sum to 41,158,275.29 of the 42,981,164.82-DOLA non-Frontier debt denominator (95.8%). Each of these markets pairs its named stablecoin with DOLA itself inside a Curve pool, so roughly half of the posted collateral value is endogenous DOLA rather than an independent external asset, and liquidation proceeds from these markets are reflexively priced off DOLA's own peg rather than an outside reference; this downgrades both COLLATERALIZATION PARAMETERS and LIQUIDATION MECHANICS from adequate to limited. Separately, the Frontier Fed's 2,749,310.09 DOLA of outstanding legacy debt (ctoken totalBorrows, ~2.75M DOLA, unchanged from the 2022 exploit) remains unresolved with no established repayment path beyond the slow, revenue-dependent DBR-auction route, while the jrDOLA first-loss vault backstop remains negligible (~615 DOLA against the debt base per the 2026-07-20 on-chain read, i.e. essentially zero coverage). An unresolved ~2.75M-DOLA bad-debt overhang against a first-loss buffer that rounds to zero downgrades SHUTDOWN AND BAD DEBT from limited to weak.

liquidationCapacityRatio.rationale: FiRM liquidations are funded by permissionless external liquidators who repay DOLA debt in exchange for collateral plus the market liquidation incentive; there is no DOLA-dedicated pool contractually committed to fund liquidation repayments. The jrDOLA first-loss vault absorbs post-liquidation bad-debt shortfalls (evidenced under the backstop component; ~615 DOLA at block 25572058) rather than funding liquidations, so no committed liquidation-capacity ratio exists.

overlays.notes: Measured at finalized Ethereum block 25571938 via public RPC https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com (eth_call). The Aave Umbrella documentation establishes that Umbrella is Aave's automated safety module: staked assets are burned/slashed to cover protocol deficits in the same asset-network pair without governance intervention, GHO staking is supported on Ethereum, a governance-configured per-asset deficit offset lets the DAO absorb a first tranche before stakers, and unstaking requires a 20-day cooldown plus a 2-day withdrawal window. The BGD design proposal establishes that stkGHO is the main coverage asset for GHO bad debt inside a GHO-specific Safety Pool, that slashing is automated and precise, that each stk asset defines its exchange rate as a function of slashing, and that multiple staked assets covering GHO would be slashed proportionally. The GHO facilitator documentation establishes that underlying GHO is minted by governance-approved facilitators (Aave V3, CCIP, GSM, flashmint) under governance-set bucket capacities rather than by an stkGHO-local vault system. On-chain at the pinned block: asset() on 0x4f827a63755855cdf3e8f3bcd20265c833f15033 returned GHO 0x40D16FC0246aD3160Ccc09B8D0D3A2cD28aE6C2f; totalSupply() returned 14,553,497.911194915956083757 stkGHO; convertToAssets(totalSupply) returned exactly the same integer, an underlying conversion ratio of 1.0. Blockscout's verified-contract read names the proxy a TransparentUpgradeableProxy with implementation 0x75e8aC0c063B6966E2A9954adEdf39BdE9370197 (UmbrellaStakeToken), consistent with the staking-receipt design. collateralizationParameters and liquidationMechanics are structurally not applicable: the wrapper originates no borrower debt and runs no collateral liquidation pool, so both CDP ratios are null with cited not-applicable rationales rather than measured numbers. Backstop is limited: the holder's own stake is the first-loss capital for GHO deficits, and the only deeper layer evidenced is the governance-configured deficit offset, which is a sized first-tranche buffer rather than an unconditional recapitalization commitment. Branch isolation is limited: Umbrella documents slashing isolation to the GHO-Ethereum pair, but the GHO deficits it absorbs arise from a shared multi-facilitator issuance system whose bucket caps provide only bounded isolation. Shutdown and bad-debt handling is limited: the documented path is automated slashing and burn of this very token plus emergency mechanisms, with no evidenced facility that recapitalizes stkGHO holders after a deficit. Structural redemption is limited: convertToAssets(totalSupply) is 1:1 and permissionless in design, but redemption is time-gated by the documented 20-day cooldown and 2-day window and remains slash-impaired during that period; this makes no claim about GHO's own exit quality. NOT established: the current deficit-offset size for the GHO pair, any max slashable percentage bound (getter calls reverted at the pinned block), the share of GHO facilitator debt actually covered by the stkGHO stake, and any commitment beyond the documented offset that would absorb deficits ahead of stakers.

collateralizationRatio.rationale: stkGHO is a staking receipt over GHO and originates no borrower collateral positions; the underlying GHO is minted by facilitators against heterogeneous shared lending markets, so no stkGHO collateralization ratio exists.

liquidationCapacityRatio.rationale: stkGHO operates no collateral-liquidation pool; its slashing is deficit coverage of the underlying GHO system, not liquidation of borrower collateral.

collateralizationParameters.rationale: stkGHO is an ERC-4626-style staking receipt over GHO and has no local MCR/LTV or collateral-pricing parameters.

liquidationMechanics.rationale: The wrapper creates no borrower positions and liquidates no collateral; automated slashing for deficit coverage is not a collateral liquidation mechanism.

The docs registry (contracts page) enumerates 12 markets; the MarketCreator event set confirmed by prior Pharos control reviews adds the msETH/WETH market, giving the complete set of 13 isMinter markets. For each market I read totalCollateral(), collatDecimals(), collatOracle().latestAnswer(true), MarketViewer.totalDebt(market) (which the verified MarketViewer source defines as badDebt + totalDebtShares x current debt index), maxLTV(), liquidationThreshold() and badDebt(). Per-market maxLTV is 72-90% and liquidation thresholds 76-91.5%; every market reports badDebt() = 0. Collateral value sums to 4,514,306.16 USD at each market's own oracle price; total market debt is 3,438,780.85 USG, giving collateralizationRatio 1.312764 = collateral value over total market debt. Denominator note: USG totalSupply is 43,438,453.33, but the holder list shows exactly 20,000,000 USG sitting idle in each of the two peg keeper contracts (mintPegKeeper pre-minted inventory, PegKeeperV2 debt() = 0, i.e. none of it has been deployed into the pools); supply minus this inventory is 3,438,453.33, reconciling with market debt within 327.52 USG (0.01%), so market debt is the economically outstanding USG. The conservative total-supply denominator gives 0.103924 and is recorded in analogousMetrics. The msETH/WETH market moved from staged (zero debt cap, zero debt at block 25531905) to live with 463,482.69 USG debt, so all 13 markets now carry debt. The two peg pools hold 475,846.98 USDC and 550,087.44 frxUSD of counterparty assets (recorded in analogousMetrics, not counted as borrower collateral). Liquidation mechanics per the health docs: anyone may repay an underwater loan's USG debt and take the collateral at a profit (20% fee on positive liquidation profit minted to the fee treasury, per the verified market source), collateral can be sold through the zapping proxy, and Tangent runs its own liquidation bot so liquidations proceed even when externally unprofitable; no Stability Pool or other committed capital pool exists anywhere in the reviewed contracts, so backstop is weak. Bad debt per the health docs: the DAO seizes underwater collateral to the fee treasury, bad debt is registered market-locally, anyone can burn USG via repayBadDebt, and the affected market's interest and earnings are redirected to recovery until repaid; there is no unconditional recapitalization commitment and no documented global shutdown, so shutdownAndBadDebt is limited. Branch isolation is adequate: 13 isolated markets with per-market debt caps (maxMarketDebt), market-local bad debt and market-local earnings recovery, all read on-chain. Structural redemption is weak: the overview and peg-stability docs state explicitly that USG does not use redemptions and cannot be redeemed for its collateral; the peg rests on Peg Keepers (crvUSD-fork, permissionless deposit/withdraw against USG/USDC and USG/frxUSD pools) plus price-dependent interest and rewards deduction. NOT established: position-level collateral weights per market (only aggregate protocol-priced values), any committed liquidation or insurance capital (none found), any redemption or hard peg-floor path (docs explicitly disclaim it), and DAO multisig control parameters (out of scope for this component set; the owner Safe's pause and parameter powers were only verified in the separate Pharos control review, not re-derived here).

The fee treasury receives liquidation fees and interest but is not contractually committed to debt offset; residual bad debt is handled by DAO seizure and permissionless repayBadDebt burns, evidenced under shutdownAndBadDebt.

overlays.notes: Reviewed 2026-07-20. Measured on Ethereum via the Curve official crvUSD markets API (fetch_on_chain, the backend of the crvUSD/Llamalend UI) cross-checked with an eth_call crvUSD.totalSupply() at finalized block 25576275. The nine Ethereum crvUSD mint markets held aggregate collateral 64,591,557.26 USD against aggregate borrower debt 33,455,016.14 crvUSD, giving collateralizationRatio 1.930699 (1.968426 including the 1,262,153.63 crvUSD of soft-liquidated collateral currently sitting in the LLAMMA AMMs). crvUSD totalSupply was 2,089,809,204.98 at that block, far above mint-market debt because most crvUSD is pre-minted into PegKeeper-paired stableswap pools, the FlashLender, and Llamalend lending markets rather than circulating as CDP debt (DefiLlama circulating ~225M); this overlay's collateralizationRatio is scoped to the crvUSD mint/Controller markets, the CDP minting facility. collateralizationParameters is adequate: per-market loan_discount and liquidation_discount (measured, e.g. WBTC 9e16/6e16, WETH 1.429e17/9.21e16, tBTC 9e16/6e16), AMM amplification A (measured 75-100), per-market debt ceilings (measured up to 200,000,000), and delayed-oracle routing are documented and governance-mutable, but there is no protocol-enforced minimum health beyond the owner-chosen band range. liquidationMechanics is adequate: LLAMMA performs continuous soft-liquidation, converting collateral into crvUSD band-by-band through external arbitrage as the oracle price crosses a position's bands, with hard liquidation available below the health threshold and no keeper-auction latency; the design is oracle-delayed and arbitrage-driven. liquidationCapacityRatio is structurally not applicable: LLAMMA rebalancing and hard-liquidation are funded by external arbitrageurs and keepers, not by a crvUSD-dedicated pool contractually committed to debt offset (matching the USDD, ZCHF, and DAI precedents). backstop is limited: the soft-liquidation design materially reduces bad-debt probability, but crvUSD mint markets carry no dedicated reserve or stability-pool backstop capital and no gov-token recapitalization path for a mint-market shortfall. branchIsolation is adequate: each collateral has its own isolated Controller/LLAMMA market with an independent debt ceiling (measured across 9 markets), so a shortfall is bounded to its market. shutdownAndBadDebt is limited: crvUSD has no global-settlement or emergency-shutdown (End) module; the admin and emergency_admin can pause PegKeepers and kill markets, but a mint-market shortfall is carried as under-backing without automatic recapitalization. structuralRedemption is limited: crvUSD holders have no direct redemption claim on collateral; the peg is defended by PegKeepers that mint or absorb crvUSD into Curve stableswap pools (measured: the crvUSD/USDT keeper had 33,750,000 crvUSD deployed) bounded by pool depth and PegKeeperRegulator debt limits. NOT established: the per-market health distribution and whether any position is currently in bad debt were not enumerated; oracle-manipulation resistance under thin-liquidity stress was not tested; the non-Ethereum mint markets (Arbitrum, Base, Fraxtal, etc.) were not measured; and PegKeeper pool depth under a sustained depeg was not measured.

overlays.notes: Reviewed 2026-07-20. Measured on BSC at block ~111154135 via journaled eth_call reads against the Lista Vat (0x33A34eAB3ee892D40420507B820347b1cA2201c4) plus the per-ilk GemJoin and Spot contracts from the developer registry. Vat.debt() = 24,622,565.46 lisUSD of internal credit and, critically, Vat.vice() = 2,821,803.63 lisUSD of realized, uncovered system bad debt = 11.46% of internal credit; this is a measured adverse fact and the anchor of the conservative ratings below. Enumerating the per-ilk GemJoin balances valued at each ilk's on-chain Spot*mat price gave aggregate CDP collateral 314,713,592.63 USD against enumerated ilk debt 21,796,591.81 lisUSD (aggregate collateralizationRatio 14.4387). That aggregate is high because collateral utilization is low: users deposit far more collateral than they borrow (e.g. the slisBNB ilk holds ~202M USD of collateral against only ~1.46M debt), while the dominant ceaBNBc ilk carries 89% of CDP debt at a 5.39 ratio. The risk-relevant measured fact is therefore the 11.46% realized bad debt, not the headline ratio. BSC lisUSD totalSupply was 75,097,217.50, well above Vat.debt because lisUSD is a cross-chain LayerZero OFT and because PSM pre-mint and D3M/AMO credit-minting expand supply without CDP collateral. collateralizationParameters is adequate: per-ilk liquidation ratios mat (measured 1.1-3.0) and debt ceilings line are enforced on-chain and governance-set. liquidationMechanics is limited rather than adequate: the documented Dutch auctions (10% penalty, tip/chip keeper rewards, tau/tail/cusp restart) rely on Lista-whitelisted bots and, for positions over $1M or after repeated failures, a manually team-activated community Liquidation Zone; the measured 2.82M of realized bad debt is direct evidence that liquidations did not fully protect the system. backstop is weak: there is measured uncovered bad debt in the Vat and no gov-token recapitalization mechanism is documented, while D3M/AMO credit-mint lisUSD into Aave/Venus without collateral. branchIsolation is adequate: each collateral is an isolated ilk with its own mat, line, and Clipper (measured), so risk admission is bounded per ilk, though losses mutualize in the shared Vow. shutdownAndBadDebt is limited: no emergency-shutdown or global-settlement mechanism is documented and the measured bad debt is simply carried in the Vat/Vow. structuralRedemption is limited: the PSM offers 1:1 lisUSD-to-USDT/USDC redemption but is capped at 500,000 lisUSD/day at a 2% fee (documented), and holders have no direct claim on vault collateral. liquidationCapacityRatio is structurally not applicable: liquidations are externally funded Dutch auctions and community liquidators, with no lisUSD-dedicated pool contractually committed to debt offset. NOT established: the split of each GemJoin balance between locked ink and unlocked free gem (so the aggregate collateralizationRatio is an upper bound on actively-borrowed collateralization), the PSM and D3M/AMO ilk debt outside the enumerated gemjoins, the cross-chain distribution of the OFT supply, and whether the 2.82M vice is being actively worked down.
